newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Panama reach open skies aviation agreement.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Panama reach open skies aviation agreement.

text.p: The United States and Panama have reached an open-skies aviation agreement, allowing airlines of both countries to operate without restriction to and beyond each other's countries, the U.S. Transportation Department said on Friday.
It is the first open-skies agreement for the United States in Latin America, the department said.
The pact contains the same provisions as open-skies agreements that the United States has concluded in Europe and, recently, in Asia, the department said in a statement.
"This first open-skies agreement in Latin America represents the opening of an important market for U.S. citizens, businesses and airlines," Transportation Secretary Rodney Slater said.

Slater also said it would help Panama and Central America develop their economic resources and tourism, and emphasized the importance to the United States of extending open skies in Latin America, saying it would result in lower fares.
He said U.S. officials will meet with the government of Chile on April 9 and 10 in Santiago to discuss an open-skies agreement.
